title: Artificial Intelligence in Academic Writing: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation of a Hands-On Workshop Among Healthcare Professionals and Students
content: Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support literature discovery, manuscript preparation, and evidence synthesis, but effective use depends on practical skills and an understanding of research integrity. This study evaluated participants’ perceptions of an eight-hour, hands-on workshop on AI-assisted academic writing. Methods: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based evaluation included 64 of 80 registered delegates. The validated questionnaire contained demographic items, Likert-scale statements, nominal-response items, and open-ended questions. Quantitative responses were summarized descriptively, and qualitative feedback was analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic framework. Results: Before the workshop, 16 participants (25.0%) agreed or strongly agreed that they had a good understanding of AI applications in academic writing, whereas 54 (84.4%) agreed or strongly agreed that their understanding had improved after the workshop. Forty-five participants (70.3%) reported confidence in using AI tools after the workshop, and 44 (68.8%) planned to use them in future academic writing. Qualitative feedback emphasized practical exposure, time-saving applications, and greater awareness of ethical use. Conclusions: Participants reported improved understanding, confidence, and awareness of responsible AI use after the workshop. Structured, practice-oriented AI literacy training may support the responsible integration of AI into academic work, although objective pre-post competency testing is needed in future studies.
